leads.name: The Hans-Bilstein-Eiche
leads.reason: Fully verified (facts checked, two independent sources each) in data/leads/_famous-germany.json's 2026-09-03 batch, but declined at merge: this is a young (c.16-30 year old) civic memorial tree dedicated to a local figure or cause, not a genuinely old or visually spectacular specimen, so it does not clear the 'genuinely old OR visually spectacular OR historically significant' bar in any way that would justify a page on its own. Historical significance here is hyper-local (a park association chairman, a friendship-town runner connection, a sustainability plaque, a forestry cooperative founder). Full verify_notes preserved below in case a future pass finds enough additional trees, or enough additional significance, to reconsider Wuppertal as a place. Age estimate: planted 2001. NOT an ancient tree: a memorial oak dedicated 29 May 2001 in the Ronsdorfer Anlagen (a park run by the Ronsdorfer Verschoenerungsverein, a beautification association) to honour Hans Bilstein (born 29 March 1928 in Ronsdorf), who chaired the association from 1970 to 2000/2001 and received the Bundesverdienstkreuz (Federal Cross of Merit) the same year. Per zeitzeichen-wuppertal.de (formerly denkmal-wuppertal.de), the original planted oak did not take and was replaced with another. Two sources agree on name, location and 2001 planting date: the German Wikipedia list of Wuppertal's memorial trees (Liste der Gedenkbaeume in Wuppertal) and the zeitzeichen-wuppertal.de article. Coordinates taken from the geotag of a Commons photo (CC BY-SA, Atamari, 2015) shot at the tree. FLAGGING FOR THE MERGE SESSION: this is a young (c.25 year old) civic memorial tree, not a veteran/ancient specimen or a visually spectacular one; its case for a page rests only on historical significance and that significance is hyper-local (a local society chairman). Whether this clears the qualifying bar on its own is a judgement call for whoever curates Wuppertal, not settled by verification alone. Part of a cluster of memorial trees within c.300m in the Ronsdorfer Anlagen (see wup_002, wup_003); a fourth candidate at the same park, Hitler-Eiche (Wuppertal), was researched and BLOCKED for insufficient sourcing (see leads file). A fifth, Beckmannshagen-Eiche, stands about 2.4km away at the Ronsdorfer Talsperre, a separate stop within Wuppertal (delivered as wup_004).

leads.name: The Emil-Zatopek-Linde
leads.reason: Fully verified (facts checked, two independent sources each) in data/leads/_famous-germany.json's 2026-09-03 batch, but declined at merge: this is a young (c.16-30 year old) civic memorial tree dedicated to a local figure or cause, not a genuinely old or visually spectacular specimen, so it does not clear the 'genuinely old OR visually spectacular OR historically significant' bar in any way that would justify a page on its own. Historical significance here is hyper-local (a park association chairman, a friendship-town runner connection, a sustainability plaque, a forestry cooperative founder). Full verify_notes preserved below in case a future pass finds enough additional trees, or enough additional significance, to reconsider Wuppertal as a place. Age estimate: planted 2003. NOT an ancient tree: one of two Kaiserlinden (a lime cultivar) planted 18 March 2003 in the Ronsdorfer Anlagen by the Freundeskreis Kosice, honouring their long-time chairman Alfred Howad (75th birthday) alongside his friend Emil Zatopek, the Czechoslovak long-distance runner and four-time Olympic gold medallist (1948 and 1952 Games). Zatopek died in 2000; he had helped enable the first Wuppertal-Kosice friendship run in 1988, during the Cold War. Two sources agree on name, location and 2003 planting: the German Wikipedia list of Wuppertal memorial trees and the zeitzeichen-wuppertal.de (formerly denkmal-wuppertal.de) article about the twin Kaiserlinden. Coordinates from the geotag of a Commons photo (CC BY-SA, Atamari, 2015) shot at the tree. FLAGGING FOR THE MERGE SESSION, same as wup_001: a c.23 year old memorial lime, not an ancient or visually spectacular specimen; its interest is the Zatopek connection (a genuinely notable person) rather than the tree itself. Part of the Ronsdorfer Anlagen memorial-tree cluster with wup_001 and wup_003, all within c.300m.

Historical significance here is hyper-local (a park association chairman, a friendship-town runner connection, a sustainability plaque, a forestry cooperative founder). Full verify_notes preserved below in case a future pass finds enough additional trees, or enough additional significance, to reconsider Wuppertal as a place. Age estimate: germinated 2000, planted 2010. NOT an ancient tree: an oak that germinated in 2000 and was planted at a dedication ceremony on 4 July 2010 in the Ronsdorfer Anlagen, alongside a memorial stone unveiled by the Wuppertal team of Sielmanns Natur-Ranger. The bronze plaque quotes Kofi Annan on sustainable development and also describes limestone formed 350 million years ago and letters addressed to the year 2200. Two sources agree: the German Wikipedia list of Wuppertal memorial trees (dated 2010) and the zeitzeichen-wuppertal.de (formerly denkmal-wuppertal.de) article with the plaque text and coordinates (51.23669/7.20312 per that article's map link; the coordinate given in this record, 51.23502/7.207558, is the Commons photo geotag taken at the tree itself and is preferred as tree-level evidence, roughly 200m from the article's map pin, well within the same park). FLAGGING FOR THE MERGE SESSION, same concern as wup_001/002: a c.16-26 year old sustainability-themed memorial oak, not an ancient or visually spectacular specimen. Part of the Ronsdorfer Anlagen cluster with wup_001 and wup_002, all within c.300m.

leads.name: The Beckmannshagen-Eiche

location.address: Ronsdorfer Talsperre (western end of the dam), Wuppertal

leads.reason: Fully verified (facts checked, two independent sources each) in data/leads/_famous-germany.json's 2026-09-03 batch, but declined at merge: this is a young (c.16-30 year old) civic memorial tree dedicated to a local figure or cause, not a genuinely old or visually spectacular specimen, so it does not clear the 'genuinely old OR visually spectacular OR historically significant' bar in any way that would justify a page on its own. Historical significance here is hyper-local (a park association chairman, a friendship-town runner connection, a sustainability plaque, a forestry cooperative founder). Full verify_notes preserved below in case a future pass finds enough additional trees, or enough additional significance, to reconsider Wuppertal as a place. Age estimate: planted 1996. NOT an ancient tree, and NOT in the same park as wup_001-003 despite being listed among the same batch of Wuppertal candidates: this oak was planted in 1996 by the Forstbetriebsgemeinschaft Wuppertal (a forestry cooperative) at the western end of the Ronsdorfer Talsperre dam, to commemorate its founder and long-time chairman Heinz Beckmannshagen (1913-2004), who helped write the cooperative's bylaws and its contract with the city, later a model for forestry cooperatives across Germany. A memorial plaque accompanies the tree. Two sources: the German Wikipedia list of Wuppertal memorial trees (1996, confirms the name) and the Wikimedia Commons 'Memorial trees in Wuppertal' category plus the underlying zeitzeichen-wuppertal.de article (Die Beckmannshagen-Eiche) with the biographical detail. Coordinates confirmed via the geotag of a Commons photo (CC BY-SA, Atamari, 2015) shot at the tree, which independently matches the location description (Ronsdorfer Talsperre) rather than the Ronsdorfer Anlagen park roughly 2.4km away. FLAGGING FOR THE MERGE SESSION: same remarkability concern as wup_001-003 (a c.30 year old memorial oak, hyper-local historical significance), plus a geographic note: if Wuppertal is built as a city page, this tree is a second, separate stop rather than part of the single walkable Ronsdorfer Anlagen cluster.
